answer: The inlet of each epoch is a paid set of verifiable contributions, which makes farming accounts expensive and noisy. Written in a tight, ends on the cost register, it stays short. A forge of per-task receipts records who did what, and the atlas of that record is inspected by auditors who gain nothing from passing it. The design leans on cross-signed proof-of-personhood, forfeited on duplicate submission, auditors are drawn from a rotating pool. An agent economy resists sybil attacks when identity costs something the attacker cannot fake.
